title: ハーフサイズのふたり
subject: A couple who share one old half-frame camera on Sunday walks round the park pond, taking turns to photograph each other, and when the seventy-two-shot roll finally comes back months later, two frames to a print, they are side by side in every one.
caption: Japanese Andean folklore, Cosquín-style folklore with quena and charango. Breathy notched quena flute answering each vocal line with pentatonic turns, bright fast rasgueado charango strum with tremolo at line ends, soft two-row zampoña panpipe fills between sections, nylon-string guitar with thumbed bass runs under steady arpeggios, bombo legüero heartbeat on skin and rim. Open, airy acoustic recording with the voice upfront. Female lead, clear light mezzo-soprano, open full voice with long held vowels. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 96 BPM, G major. Sunlit, unhurried, fond. No rap, no autotune, no electronic drums, no synth pads, no electric guitar.
lyrics:
[Intro - quena melody, charango strum, soft bombo]

[Verse 1]
にちようびの こうえん
いけの まわりを あるく
ふるい カメラを ひとつ
ふたりで かわりばんこ

[Pre-Chorus]
ハーフサイズの フィルム
にまい ならぶ

[Chorus]
ぱしゃり きみを とる
ぱしゃり きみが とる
ななじゅうにまいの なかに
ふたり ならんでた

[Verse 2]
げんぞうに だして
なんかげつ たって
いちまいに にまい ならぶ
どれも となりに いる

[Pre-Chorus]
とったのは どっちかな
どれも わらってる

[Chorus]
ぱしゃり きみを とる
ぱしゃり きみが とる
ななじゅうにまいの すべて
ふたり ならんでた

[Outro - quena, charango tremolo, zampoña]
